title: Universal Agentic Skill Format v1.0
description: Structural schema for the Universal Skill Format manifest proposed in the OWASP Agentic Skills Top 10 whitepaper, AST10 (Cross-Platform Reuse). This file constrains SHAPE only -- types, required keys, enumerations, and the syntax of the version/hash/signature fields. Permission SEMANTICS (default-deny network precedence, deny_write-wins-over-write, no wildcards in permissions.files, identity-file protection, and risk_tier validated against the declared permission set) are NOT expressible here and are enforced by validators/usf.py. A manifest that passes this schema is well-formed, not policy-conformant.

^x-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$.description: Vendor extension namespace. The format is a superset of platform-specific manifests, so a runtime may carry extra metadata -- but only under an explicit x- prefix. Every other unknown key is rejected: a typo such as `deny_writes` that silently drops identity-file protection is the exact manifest-stripping failure AST10 describes.

name.description: Lowercase package identifier. Must match the platform-native skill name (for example the SKILL.md frontmatter `name`); validators/usf.py checks that cross-format agreement when given the skill directory.

platforms.description: Runtimes this package is declared compatible with. Adding one is a re-validation event, not an edit: AST10's premise is that security properties are lost in translation between runtimes.

identity.description: Decentralized identity anchor. Optional, because a manifest that ships unsigned has no key to anchor; validators/usf.py warns when it is absent rather than accepting a DID that resolves to nothing.

files.description: All three lists are required even when empty. A declared-empty list and an absent list are the same thing to a permissive target runtime, which is precisely the AST10 implicit-privilege-escalation path; requiring the key forces the author to state the floor.

allow.description: Domain allowlist, not a boolean. An empty list means no egress at all -- it does not mean unrestricted.

deny.description: Kept for explicit auditability only. Evaluation is default-deny, so the sole meaningful value is the literal "*"; validators/usf.py rejects anything else, because treating deny as an override list inverts the precedence rule.

shell.description: Explicit shell access declaration. Never inferred.

risk_tier.description: L0=safe, L1=low, L2=elevated, L3=destructive. An untrusted author assertion: validators/usf.py independently derives a floor from the declared permission set and rejects under-declaration.

signature.description: ed25519 over the RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON serialization of this manifest, excluding the `signature` field and including `content_hash`. The literal "unsigned" is a valid, explicit declaration -- validators/usf.py reports it as signature_state="unsigned", a policy decision for the consumer, not a malformed manifest.

content_hash.description: sha256 over the complete skill package.

platform.description: Closed enumeration. A free-text or "other" platform value would reintroduce the normalization gap the format exists to close.

pathList.description: Explicit paths only. The no-wildcard and no-traversal rules are enforced semantically by validators/usf.py so the rejection carries a precise reason rather than a regex failure.

host.description: Bare lowercase hostname. Host-only matching: no scheme, no port, no path, no wildcard subdomains. Enforced semantically by validators/usf.py.
